1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night
It had been raining in Peñaseca for three days. That spring, Lucía Romero’s older sister had left for Madrid, and since then Lucía had been running the village’s small apothecary alone.
As night fell, she closed the shutters, tallied up the day’s earnings, blew out the lamp, and went upstairs.
She had just lain down when someone knocked loudly at the door below. A man’s voice called out, “Is anyone there?”
On the threshold stood a young man, soaked to the bone, his left arm wrapped in a bloodstained cloth. He said his name was Diego Lobo and that he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
“I need medical attention,” Lobo said quietly. “I can pay. Will three thousand five hundred reales be enough?”
He pulled a letter wrapped in waxed paper from his jacket. “This letter must reach the San Blas monastery before the eighteenth of May.”
Treating the wound would be child’s play for Lucía, but the letter unsettled her.
Still, she refused his money and only said, “I’ll take you to the mountains at dawn.”
2: They set off at daybreak. Lucía carried a basket on her back with bread, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the slope, they came across old Tomás Gil, who was splitting firewood. He set down his axe and told them in a low voice that the evening before, three strangers had asked at the village entrance about a wounded young man.
"Take the path, Lucía," said Tomás Gil. "The main road isn’t safe." Lucía thanked him.
The path was narrow and slippery. Lucía led the way, stepping firmly with each stride. Lobo followed in silence.
By midday, the rain had stopped, the mist slowly lifted, and in the distance, the roof of San Blas Monastery came into view. At the door, a nun, Sister Inés, waited to receive visitors.
Sister Inés took the letter, examined the red seal, and nodded. "The abbess has been waiting two years for this letter."
Lobo said to Lucía, "I owe you my life." Lucía smiled. "Then next time you come, fix the roof of my apothecary." Lobo stayed at the monastery.
At dusk, Lucía descended the mountain alone. By the time she reached home, night had fallen. She lit the lamp and sat behind the counter for a long while.
